checks.name: Source direction
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test codegen -- --nocapture && head -3 sdk/typescript/packages/protocol/generated/spike.ts && grep -n 'generated/spike.ts' sdk/typescript/packages/protocol/conformance/negative/*.ts sdk/typescript/packages/protocol/conformance/spike-runtime.ts
checks.output: generated/spike.ts (108 lines, 27 exports) is written by the Rust test from automonique_protocol::codegen::emit_typescript(&hostile_slice()); it carries the marker 'GENERATED by automonique_protocol::codegen' and 'Rust is the wire source of truth'. All five hand-written TypeScript files in the spike (4 negative conformance cases plus spike-runtime.ts) import every wire type from ../generated/spike.ts; none declares a competing SessionId, TurnId, MessageKind, Sequence, TurnOutcome, ApprovalDecision, RunState, KnownEvent or DecodedEvent. Near-miss not recorded in VERDICT.md: hostile_slice() is a hand-authored SpikeSchema literal inside codegen.rs, so the slice's bounds (SessionId 128, TurnId 64, MessageKind 64, Sequence 0..i64::MAX) are literals rather than read from the real protocol domains in provider.rs (ProviderSessionId, ProviderTurnId). The direction Rust -> TypeScript holds; the link from the real wire types to the slice does not exist.

checks.name: Slice difficulty
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test codegen slice_difficulty && grep -n 'export type\|export const\|export interface' sdk/typescript/packages/protocol/generated/spike.ts
checks.output: The emitted surface contains every construct the contract demands: bounded string MessageKind_MAX_BYTES = 64; bounded integer Sequence_MIN = 0n / Sequence_MAX = 9223372036854775807n; two branded domains SessionId (128 bytes) and TurnId (64 bytes); the TurnOutcome union with three variants of which 'cancelled' is payload-free and 'completed'/'failed' carry payloads; both enum classes (ApprovalDecision as SecuritySensitive, RunState as ReadOnly); the optional/nullable pair 'readonly note?: string' versus 'readonly detail: string | null'; and an unseen event path with MAX_UNKNOWN_EVENT_BYTES = 4096.

checks.name: Bound preservation
checks.command: bun sdk/typescript/packages/protocol/conformance/spike-runtime.ts && npx --offline tsc --noEmit --strict --ignoreConfig --target ES2023 --lib ES2023,DOM --module ESNext --moduleResolution Bundler --allowImportingTsExtensions conformance/negative/bound-widening.ts
checks.output: bun 1.3.13 ran the runtime half and printed 'all runtime property checks passed' with exit 0. It asserts the exact limit is accepted and one byte over is refused for both branded domains and for the bounded integer at the signed 64-bit ceiling (Sequence_MAX and Sequence_MAX + 1n, plus -1n), that an empty identifier is refused, and that a multibyte string of TurnId_MAX_BYTES 'e-acute' characters is refused because the bound is measured in UTF-8 bytes rather than UTF-16 code units. At the type level, bound-widening.ts fails with 'error TS2322: Type \'string\' is not assignable to type \'TurnId\'', so a raw string cannot bypass the validator; the generated types are not widened to bare string/number.

checks.name: Brand distinctness
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --locked --test codegen -- --nocapture; cd sdk/typescript/packages/protocol && npx --offline tsc --noEmit --strict --ignoreConfig --target ES2023 --lib ES2023,DOM --module ESNext --moduleResolution Bundler --allowImportingTsExtensions conformance/negative/brand-crossing.ts; bun ./conformance/spike-runtime.ts
checks.output: Recorded as the partial it is. Compile time (unchanged, re-measured): brand-crossing.ts exits 2 with 'error TS2322: Type \'TurnId\' is not assignable to type \'SessionId\'' and the nested reason 'Type \'"TurnId"\' is not assignable to type \'"SessionId"\''. Runtime (now measured rather than probed by hand): conformance/spike-runtime.ts checks that TurnId("abc") is typeof "string", that its __brand property reads undefined, that (TurnId("abc") as string) === (SessionId("abc") as string) is true, and that it serializes as the bare string "abc"; it prints 'brand-runtime-existence: erased' and exits 0 under bun 1.3.13. VERDICT.md now records 'Brand distinctness | partial', names the erasure with the measured facts, adds constraint 6 stating what it costs R8B (no runtime domain question is answerable, so re-validate at every trust boundary with the generated constructor and never key dispatch, equality or storage on the brand), and adds a section 'Why the brand is not carried into the value' recording the decision not to change the emitter: a JS primitive cannot hold a property (assignment throws TypeError in a module), so carrying a brand needs boxing, which makes typeof "object", breaks ===, Map/Set keys and object keys in every consumer, and costs an allocation per identifier on the per-event decode path. Three tests in tests/codegen.rs enforce it and 13 of 13 pass: a_brand_that_erases_at_runtime_is_recorded_as_a_partial derives the obligation from the emitted constructors (a body ending in 'return value as {name}' cannot carry a brand) and then requires the table cell to read exactly 'partial', the row to name the runtime erasure and the constraints section to name brand and runtime; the_verdict_is_recorded_and_names_its_outcome now parses each property's Result cell and refuses any word outside pass/partial/fail/null, and requires anything short of 'pass' to also reach the constraints list; what_the_runtime_measures_agrees_with_the_emitted_brand runs the script and asserts the printed measurement equals what the emitter's text implies. Negative controls run, each observed: cell back to 'pass' -> 'the brands of ["SessionId", "TurnId"] exist only in the type checker ... but the verdict records "pass"'; cell set to 'mostly' -> 'Brand distinctness records "mostly", which is not one of ["pass", "partial", "fail", "null"]'; constraint 6 deleted -> 'no constraint tells R8B what the runtime erasure costs it'; measurement line renamed -> 'the runtime conformance script no longer reports whether the brand survives into the value'; measurement inverted -> 'the emitted constructors say the brand is erased, but running the generated code under bun reports carried'; emitter changed to return Object.assign(new String(value), {__brand}) -> the three runtime checks failed with 'typeof is object', '__brand is TurnId' and 'no longer compare equal', the partial obligation correctly deactivated, and the zero-diff test caught the stale file. The emitter was restored and sdk/typescript/packages/protocol/generated/spike.ts hashes dd875a6b743ed5ab8d27d0cc26a0ae41c09485cbdf1730719f46110f31270aeb again, unchanged by this work.

checks.name: Union exhaustiveness
checks.output: union-nonexhaustive.ts fails with 'error TS2345: Argument of type \'{ readonly kind: "cancelled"; }\' is not assignable to parameter of type \'never\'', so a switch missing the cancelled variant does not typecheck through the emitted assertNeverTurnOutcome helper. payload-free-variant.ts fails with 'error TS2339: Property \'text\' does not exist on type \'{ readonly kind: "cancelled"; }\'', so the payload-free variant did not degenerate into an optional-payload variant. Both exit 2.

checks.name: Unknown-event tolerance
checks.output: decodeEvent("turn_hibernated", '{"a":1}') returns {known: false, kind, payload}; the runtime script asserts it does not throw, that the kind 'turn_hibernated' is preserved and that the payload string is preserved byte-for-byte, and separately that a payload one byte over MAX_UNKNOWN_EVENT_BYTES (4096) throws ValidationError('event','unknown_payload_too_large') rather than silently truncating. The ReadOnly enum follows the same rule: decodeRunState("hibernated") returns {known: false, spelling: "hibernated"} while the SecuritySensitive decodeApprovalDecision("allow_always") throws 'unknown_enum_value'. Exit 0.

checks.name: Reproducibility
checks.command: sha256sum sdk/typescript/packages/protocol/generated/spike.ts; cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --test codegen; sha256sum sdk/typescript/packages/protocol/generated/spike.ts
checks.output: The checked-in file hashed dd875a6b743ed5ab8d27d0cc26a0ae41c09485cbdf1730719f46110f31270aeb before and the identical digest after the regenerating test rewrote it, so regeneration is a zero-diff operation on this tree. The Rust tests additionally regenerate eight times and compare, reverse the branded-id, enum and union-variant input order and compare, and assert the output contains no '2025-'/'2026-' date, no 'timestamp', no 'generated at' and no '/home/' path. The generator has no clock, environment or hash input at all. Recorded caveat, already named in VERDICT.md constraint 5: no CI step yet regenerates into a temporary tree and diffs; the zero-diff property is asserted by the spike's own tests plus this before/after digest comparison.

checks.name: Verdict quality
checks.command: cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml -p automonique-protocol --offline --locked --test codegen verdict_quality && cat sdk/typescript/packages/protocol/generated/VERDICT.md
checks.output: All 3 verdict_quality tests pass. VERDICT.md states '**Verdict: recommended with named constraints.**' and its opening paragraph now says four of the five properties are preserved and that brand distinctness is a partial. The table records: bound preservation pass, brand distinctness partial, union exhaustiveness pass, unknown-event tolerance pass, reproducibility pass — each with how it was measured. It lists six constraints R8B must plan for (bigint not number, byte bounds not code units, the assertNever helper, no embedded content digest because the crate has no hash implementation, the missing CI zero-diff step, and new constraint 6: the brand is compile-time only and erases in the value, with the boundary re-validation R8B must budget for). It records the same two unmeasured properties with reasons (generalization to the full protocol surface, client generation), keeps the 'What a failure would have cost' section naming R8B, and adds why an outright failure and this half-failure differ. The test no longer greps for property names: it parses each Result cell, rejects any word outside pass/partial/fail/null, and requires a non-pass result to also appear in the constraints section, so a future partial cannot be recorded as a footnote or as an undefined word.

notes: Both JavaScript toolchains the spike needs were present, so nothing was skipped for a missing runtime: bun 1.3.13 ran the runtime half and npx --offline tsc resolved TypeScript 6.0.3 from a cache with no network. The codegen test suite prints 'GAP:' lines when a runtime or tsc is unavailable; running it with --nocapture produced zero GAP lines, so the tsc-dependent negative cases, the new script typecheck and the bun runtime cases genuinely executed rather than silently returning. All ten rows now pass. Brand distinctness was closed by recording rather than by cleverness: the property really is a partial (compile-time brand, complete runtime erasure), so VERDICT.md now says partial, names the erasure, states what it costs R8B, and records why the emitter was deliberately not changed to carry the brand into the value. The emitter's output is byte-for-byte unchanged (spike.ts still hashes dd875a6b743ed5ab8d27d0cc26a0ae41c09485cbdf1730719f46110f31270aeb), so the zero-diff reproducibility property is untouched. Three tests were added (10 -> 13 in the codegen target) and every one was negative-controlled by breaking the behaviour and observing the named failure, then restoring it; the controls and their observed messages are listed in the Brand distinctness row. The obligation is derived from the emitted text rather than hard-coded, so if a later item makes the brand survive at runtime the test stops demanding the caveat instead of demanding a stale one. Quality was re-measured, not re-argued: the automonique-lab suites that were red at the previous base are green at this one.
